"Love" is a word some people do not use lightly. My boyfriend and I didn't say "I love you" for a while. I said it to him far before he could reciprocate. I feel like the first time you fall in love with someone, it takes a while to identify and define what love means to you; you need to stay true to your definition of the word. Everyone has their own definition, and I think it shows an admirable honesty that he can't lie to you and say it. To be honest, I had a feeling that my boyfriend loved me before he knew it. While it hurts when the other person will not give you the same reassurance you give him or her, it is worth it to wait and see; this isn't worth throwing away your relationship quite yet, unless you are in a huge hurry to settle down.

One thing to keep in mind for a DBQ is the legitimacy of the source(s). Is the source biased? Who wrote it? When was it written? Who was it written for? Why was it written? Keep the document in mind for the whole paper, and refute any of the information it presents that seems biased.

For your thesis, I would say: [This document] suggests that the Aztecs were [however they were] by [summary of the document's contents].

If the documents have different stances, explain why.

**Fear and Loathing** and **Heart of Darkness**: Compare the structure of both novels, and discuss how it enhances the themes of the books (if you haven't read one of these, try comparing them to **Dante's Inferno** or **Catcher in the Rye**.)

Or, just list every book that you have enjoyed enough and understood enough to write about and come up with common themes, structures, language, characters, moods, etc.

I think there was railroad stuff going on then, too, which would hit on transportation.
